note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old female with ~1 week of dysuria, urinary frequency, suprapubic aching and recent pink-tinged urine; suspected uncomplicated urinary tract infection (cystitis).

History:
- Presenting complaint: Burning/stinging on urination, increased urinary frequency, lower abdominal (suprapubic) aching worse with urination.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms present for just under one week (patient initially said a few days then clarified ~just under a week; conflict noted).
- Hematuria: Patient noticed pink-colored urine today (no quantified amount).
- Associated symptoms: No fever, no nausea/vomiting, no flank or side pain.
- Bowel/GI: Baseline irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) with variable stool consistency; no new bowel symptoms.
- Gynecologic/sexual: Sexually active with long-term boyfriend; reports no condom use (~1 week ago); on combined oral contraceptive. Last menstrual period ~2 weeks ago.
- Past medical history: IBS.
- Medications: Combined oral contraceptive — dose/route/frequency not documented; IBS medication recalled as starting with "M" — exact name and dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Previous adverse reaction to an antibiotic the patient identifies as "Clindamycin." (Clinician acknowledgement included an unclear term "Ritib" — conflict noted.)
- Social history: Lives in university halls with a flatmate; occasional alcohol; tried cannabis once ~1.5 weeks ago; does not smoke cigarettes.

Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Examination findings: none performed/documented.

Impression:
- Probable lower urinary tract infection (cystitis), uncomplicated based on history and absence of systemic features.

Plan:
- Diagnostic testing: Urine sample to be collected and dropped off at practice for point-of-care testing and laboratory culture/analysis; results will be communicated to patient.
- Empiric treatment options discussed: Trimethoprim or nitrofurantoin (nitrofurantoin described as a three-day course). Specific antibiotic, dose, route, and frequency to be determined/prescribed (not documented).
- Supportive care: Advise adequate oral hydration; paracetamol for pain as needed.
- Safety net/follow-up: Return if symptoms worsen or if fever, flank/back pain, or vomiting develop; if symptoms not improving within one week, follow-up appointment recommended.
- Counseling: Brief advice to avoid regular recreational drug use (patient-requested guidance).

document_quality (Quality checks):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, pulse, BP).
  - Physical examination findings (abdominal, costovertebral angle tenderness).
  - Urine analysis/culture results.
  - Pregnancy test result (patient on combined pill; last period 2 weeks ago).
  - Exact antibiotic prescription (choice, dose, route, frequency) and documentation of decision.
  - Full name and dose of IBS medication.
  - Details of allergic reaction to clindamycin (type/severity).
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Symptom duration: initially described as "a few days," later clarified as "just under a week" (conflict noted).
  - Allergy/medication acknowledgement: patient states allergy to "Clindamycin"; clinician response included an unclear term ("Ritib") — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Overall intelligible; occasional unclear/garbled medication words and brief overlapping speech.
